title: Trump 86s military option, insists ‘Economic D-Day’ will force Iran to capitulate
text:
‘ECONOMIC D-DAY’ COMING: As his six-week war approaches its sixth month mark, President Donald Trump has given up on bombing Iran and is counting on “economic warfare and isolation on an unprecedented scale” to break Iran’s will.

“We have very draconian sanctions, and we’ll see what happens,” Trump told reporters yesterday. In a Wednesday night post on Truth Social, Trump described the plan as “Economic D-Day,” and said it will target not just Iran, but anyone who helps Tehran in any way. “ANY country that allows its financial institutions, businesses, airports, or government entities to provide any type of lifeline to Iran will itself face TREMENDOUS Economic Consequences. Oil smuggling, swap lines, cash transfers, exchange houses, ship registries, front companies — It all needs to stop NOW,” Trump posted.

“This is going to be the greatest coordinated economic isolation in the history of the world, and we are going to them and saying, you are either with us or against us,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in an appearance on CNBC. “If you insist on doing business with them —  either transferring money, buying their oil, doing seaborne ship transport first — then the U.S. Treasury and the U.S. government will put its full might and force toward enforcing against you.”

“We are going to squash the economy of this murderous regime, which will curtail their ability to project power through their proxies,” Bessent boasted. “So it is time for our allies and the rest of the world to make a decision.”

“It is a one-two punch. We have the blockade, and we are going to have the toughest sanctions in history,” Bessent said. “I will tell you, this will work. It worked in Venezuela once we put up the blockade. It is working in Cuba right now. And it is going to work in Iran, and we are going to collapse this regime.”

THE IRAN PEACE DEAL EXPIRES — AND THE CONFLICT ENTERS A DANGEROUS PHASE

IRAN SCOFFS: Publicly at least, Iran is projecting an image of dismissive defiance. “Americans think squeezing Iran harder will win concessions that were never part of the agreement,” Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf posted on X. “Bessent and Hegseth are way out of their league. Stop waiting for the clown crew to pull a rabbit out of their hat and clean up the mess you made.”

Iran is threatening an economic D-Day of its own, reportedly planning strikes on Gulf oil terminals to surge global energy prices, and by targeting the U.S. support for so-called “dark runs” through a narrow channel on the Omani side of the Strait of Hormuz.

Marc Thiessen, a fellow at the American Enterprise Institute, warns that Iran could be planning an “October surprise” ahead of the mid-term elections, because Operation Epic Fury — while inflicting devastating losses, still left Iran with enough firepower to threaten Gulf energy infrastructure. “Iran could decide to use that firepower before Americans go to the polls in November,” Thiessen writes in the Washington Post.

Others worry that the hard-line regime, now controlled to a large extent by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, doesn’t care about the suffering of the Iranian people, so long as it can hold on to power. “Someone should inform President Trump that Iran is already the most sanctioned country in the world by far by the United States,” Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-MD) said on MS NOW. “And we do have what are called secondary sanctions on Iran where we already sanction countries that do business with Iran.”

IRAN SLAMS US ‘CLOWN CREW’ AS TRUMP THREATENS TO ANNEX STRAIT OF HORMUZ WITH NO END TO WAR IN SIGHT

TRUMP: ‘A LOT OF BOATS ARE COMING THROUGH’: Trump insists that while the U.S. naval blockade is an impenetrable “wall of steel,” the media is missing the fact that U.S. has been able to move ships through the strait surreptitiously by keeping their transponders off.

“The strait is open,” Trump said. “A lot of boats are coming through. People aren’t reporting that. And that may slow down a little bit at some point, but right now, a lot of boats are coming through.”

The reason no one has been reporting that is because it was being done in secret. “Under the operation, which has been underway for the last several weeks, 15-20 tankers have entered and exited the strait each night through a southern channel along the coast of Oman,” two U.S. officials told Axios. “About 10 million barrels of oil a day — roughly half the pre-war volume — are being transported out of the strait and injected into the global energy market, the officials said.”

“We have possession, complete control of the strait,” Trump said Wednesday. “I mean, outside of nuisance value — and there is nuisance value when they shoot a drone every once in a while, but … And over the last couple of weeks, we’ve had a lot of oil coming out, a lot of oil. It’s not going to be perfect, but it’s a lot of oil coming out, a lot.”

“I would say that Iran had been fairly effective up until now, shutting off about 90% of the flow of traffic. But we’re starting to see more traffic get in and out of there, and that’s a good thing,” Rep. Don Bacon (R-NE) said on CNN. “ I think this is a better strategy than what we have had. The blockade is probably the easier thing for us to enforce. Right now, we’ve been able to choke almost all the traffic going in and out of Iran. That’s good. Their economy is really struggling. It’s going to really weaken the regime.”

TRUMP SEEKS TO REKINDLE ‘BROMANCE’ WITH KIM: President Trump has spent the week saying nice things about North Korean dictator Kim Jong Un.

Ignoring the fact that North Korea has sent troops and missiles to help Russia in its war against Ukraine, over the weekend, Trump ordered Defense Pete Hegseth to curtail annual joint military exercises with South Korea because they “send a signal that is totally inappropriate and hostile” to North Korea, which he said, since he’s been president, “has been unthreatening and respectful.”

“I do have a good relationship with Kim Jong Un,” Trump said yesterday. “He didn’t like Biden. He didn’t like Obama. He didn’t like anybody. But he likes me.”

“I didn’t like the fact that we’re doing these massive military exercises, really, against North Korea … when I’m friendly with him,” Trump said.

Kim didn’t return the warm sentiments. Instead, Pyongyang said curtailing the drill meant nothing, and underscored the message by launching a barrage of ​​10 short-range ballistic missiles in the sea off its eastern coast.

“We think it’s not worth making comments on that and we have no interest in it at all,” said Kim’s sister, Kim Yo Jong, in a statement. “The provocative, aggressive nature of the drills won’t change even though their duration and size were reduced.”

Trump says he wants to meet with Kim Jong Un later this year, and insisted that despite possessing an arsenal of 57 nuclear warheads, North Korea is not a threat as long as he’s president. “I know Kim Jong Un very well, and he’s going to be fine. As long as we have a smart president, he’s going to be fine. If we have a dumb president, then he’s probably not going to be so fine.”

DID TRUMP REVEAL CLASSIFIED INTELLIGENCE? When Trump told reporters Wednesday that Kim “has 57 very powerful nuclear weapons,” arms control experts were surprised. “I never expected to hear a President give such a precise estimate. And I have not heard of any President since the collapse of the Agreed Framework giving an estimate of the size of North Korea’s nuclear arsenal,” David Albright, president and founder of the  Institute for Science and International Security, posted on X.

“[Intellignce Community] estimates of foreign nuclear stockpiles are basically never point estimates,” Jeffrey Lewis, an expert in nuclear nonproliferation at the Middlebury Institute of International Studies posted on X. “They’re ranges with confidence levels. Declassified documents show rounded numbers — ‘enough material for X to Y weapons ’— not individual warhead counts. ‘57’ is not how the IC talks.”

“I’d be shocked if the IC offered an individual warhead count,” Lewis said. “More likely are estimates are derived from how much [Plutonium and Highly Enriched Uranium] North Korea has produced, divided by how much material each weapon might use.”

When Trump was questioned about the number the next day he said, “I don’t want to talk about that.”

STEAMED OVER STEAM: Trump’s executive order, requiring the future aircraft carrier USS Doris Miller to be built with old-fashioned steam catapults and hydraulics, has naval ship experts scratching their heads. The carrier — which is now referred to by its hull number CVN-81, reportedly because Trump wants it named after himself — is not set to be delivered until 2034, but the redesign could further delay its construction and add billions to its cost.

“I don’t understand the silence of retired Navy Admirals who know this is all nonsense, a huge waste of money, and a major delay in completion of new ships,” retired Army Lt. Gen. Ben Hodges posted on X.

“Redesigning the USS Doris Miller, already under construction, to replace its electromagnetic catapults with steam systems will exacerbate the readiness crisis,” Bryan Clark, a senior fellow at the Hudson Institute, writes in the Washington Post. “The change is estimated to cost billions of dollars and delay the ship’s launch into the late 2030s. And that’s only if the Navy can convince a manufacturer to start building steam catapults again after a nearly three-decade hiatus.”

“The Navy adopted electromagnetic catapults in its new carriers for the same reason rail lines shifted from steam to electric propulsion during the 20th century. Electric power has fewer moving parts, is more reliable, costs less, and offers higher speeds compared with steam power,” Clark writes. “Continued construction and redesign delays for the USS Miller would shrink the fleet to nine carriers during the next decade. The Navy would need to work the smaller force harder, wearing out its people and equipment faster, and accelerating the readiness decline.”
